review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–133) and checked it against the "repeated proof machinery" rubric only. I did not search the related source roots, because the file itself had no candidate duplication. The file has two private defs (liftsMod and liftsModEquiv), one small private lemma (mem_liftsMod), and four theorems. Each theorem does a different job: the generation lemma, the freeness and orbit-counting divisibility, the p-group deduction, and the Frattini-quotient corollary. The only recurring pattern is converting between `(y i : G ⧸ N) = s i` and membership of `(y i)⁻¹ * s i` in N via `QuotientGroup.eq`. It appears in closure_range_eq_top_of_le_frattini, liftsModEquiv (twice), and indirectly in mem_liftsMod. Each use is a one-line application of an existing API lemma, so a shared helper would be a thin wrapper and would not meet the rubric. The hypothesis `∀ α ∈ H, ∀ x, (α x : G ⧸ N) = x` is repeated in signatures, but that is a statement rather than proof reasoning. isPGroup_of_le_frattini and the last corollary both reuse card_dvd_card_pow_of_le_frattini, which is already factored out. No nontrivial reasoning is duplicated across two proofs. Remaining uncertainty is small, since I did not check whether the same patterns occur in other files.
